target.title: fix(acp): preserve structured error kinds
target.body:
﻿Closes #44294

### What Problem This Solves
Currently, the ACP translator maps most gateway error kinds (like 	imeout, ate_limit, context_length, etc.) into an end_turn stop reason, losing the structured error information needed by ACP clients to correctly interpret the failure state of a prompt.

### Why This Change Was Made
By preserving the explicit error semantics from the gateway, downstream ACP clients can properly distinguish between a successful run that ended normally, one that was truncated due to token limits, and runs that outright failed due to timeout or rate limits.

### User Impact
ACP clients will now receive max_tokens as a stop reason for context length errors, and see rejected prompts via RequestError for other non-refusal errors instead of silently treating them as successful end_turn outcomes.

### Evidence
- Added/updated tests in src/acp/translator.error-kind.test.ts to assert that RequestError is correctly thrown for timeouts and unknown errors.
- Added tests validating that context_length successfully maps to max_tokens stop reason.
- Hand-tested by simulating gateway errors to ensure RequestError propagation works over ACP without breaking the protocol connection.
